theory.intro: On a speed-time graph, the **area** between the graph and the time axis is the distance travelled, because distance $=$ speed $\times$ time. Straight-line graphs make rectangles and triangles, so split the region up and add the areas.
facts: Distance travelled $=$ the **area** between the speed-time graph and the time axis.
Split that trapezium into a rectangle from the smaller speed and a triangle from the change in speed.
steps: Split the region under the graph into rectangles and triangles at each change of gradient.
Find each piece's dimensions from the graph, and calculate its area.
Add the areas together to find the total distance.

foundation.solution_text:
The region is a rectangle.
$A=15\times12$
$=180\text{ m}$

The region is a triangle.
$A=\dfrac{1}{2}\times8\times12$
$=48\text{ m}$

The region is a triangle.
$A=\dfrac{1}{2}\times5\times10$
$=25\text{ m}$

mastery.solution_text:
Car A: $A=\dfrac{1}{2}\times5\times20+20\times5+\dfrac{1}{2}\times5\times20$
$=50+100+50$
$=200\text{ m}$
Car B: $A=\dfrac{1}{2}\times4\times24+24\times8+\dfrac{1}{2}\times4\times24$
$=48+192+48$
$=288\text{ m}$
Car B travels further, by $288-200=88\text{ m}$.
